messages:
alex: heads up — saw a bunch of OTLP spans dropped/queued yesterday when eu-prod-otlp had a GC spike. traces stalled and exporter backlog grew, then we hit retry budget and started dropping. anyone else seen similar?

mira: yep saw the incident. backlog metric showed exporter_outstanding_requests spiking ~3x for ~90s. no clear reconnects; gRPC streams stayed open but stalls happened.

sam: interesting — was that the gRPC streaming path or http/protobuf fallback?

alex: mainly gRPC streaming. fallback to HTTP didn't happen automatically because deadlines weren't exceeded long enough for our timeout windows. so requests stayed stuck in the stream.

lia: proposed fix: add "stall detection" probes on the exporter side — if a request has been in-flight > X ms without any bytes/ack, mark stream degraded and trigger a short reconnect with exponential backoff + jitter.

mira: i like that. specifics matter: we need a conservative default so we don't reconnect during short pauses. maybe use sliding window of progress (bytes_sent or server-keepalive) rather than absolute time.

alex: agreed. rough config sketch i tossed together: 
```yaml
exporter: 
  protocol: grpc
  deadline_ms: 8000  # per-rpc deadline
  stall_detection_ms: 12000  # if no progress for this, consider stream stalled
  stall_probe_interval_ms: 2000  # send lightweight probe frames if available
  reconnect_policy:
    base_backoff_ms: 200
    max_backoff_ms: 60000
    jitter: full  # randomized splay to avoid thundering herd
  retry_budget:
    max_inflight: 100
    request_loss_ratio: 0.02
```

sam: small note: `stall_probe_interval_ms` can't be too chatty for high-throughput exporters. maybe make probe behavior opt-in for heavy lines, default to passive detection.

lia: also think about metrics & alerting: add exporter_stream_stall_count, exporter_reconnect_count, exporter_progress_bytes_last_10s. dashboards should surface per-region splay shows if everyone reconnects at same time.

ops-bot: alert: eu-prod-otlp exporter_reconnect_count spiked 47 in 3m at 2026-02-16T14:12:09Z

mira: good point on splay — the jitter needs to be per-host and incorporate randomized exponential backoff to avoid synchronized reconnects. i prefer a two-stage splay: small random within +-10% then full randomized between 0..base_backoff on subsequent attempts.

alex: what about HTTP fallback? if gRPC stream considered stalled, should the router immediately switch RPCs to http/protobuf for that tenant, or only after N failures?

sam: we should be conservative: do not fallback to http on first reconnect — that causes split-path semantics and can change payloads. fallback after threshold (e.g., 3 consecutive stalled reconns) and surface in logs & audit.

lia: UX for rollouts: add a console toggle per-tenant to enable aggressive stall-probes for canaries. Dev teams can opt-in when validating a new model or traffic pattern.

mira: ops concern: reconnects increase load on backend infra; so we need to add circuit breaker behavior on the backend routing layer: once region-level rejection rate > X, start shedding low-priority telemetry (metrics/infra spans) and keep sampling traces.

alex: agree. also add per-exporter token-bucket to limit reconnect rate (repairing-splay), and an admin endpoint to nudge a stream back into healthy state without full restart.

sam: tests we should add:
- simulated partial stalls where bytes stop for 10s and resume (should not fallback)
- full stalls where no progress for > stall_detection_ms (should reconnect with jitter)
- cascading reconnects test with many exporters to ensure splay prevents herd

lia: can someone draft a short RFC + config proposal? i'll wire up dashboard panels and alerts once we land on numbers.

alex: i'll start RFC draft, will include config defaults and the YAML snippet above. ping me if you want non-default settings for any tenants.

mira: sgtm. I'll add system metrics to the ingestion dashboard and a small playbook for oncall.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: exporter-stall-probe-v1 to staging (sha: a3b9c4)

sam: tiny nit — include a metric for `exporter_last_successful_send_ms` so we can compute time-since-last-progress without relying on bytes counters alone.

alex: good call. adding that. ok closing thread, will upload RFC PR in ~1h. :thumbsup:
